statement: A film starts at 17:45 and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. At what time does it end?

choices.misconception: I added 50 minutes to 45 minutes and wrote the extra 35 minutes, but forgot to add the hour that came from the 95 minutes.
I added the hours and the minutes separately and did not change 95 minutes into 1 hour and 35 minutes.
I rounded 1 hour 50 minutes up to 2 hours and forgot to take the extra 10 minutes back off.
I rounded up to 2 hours, then added 10 minutes instead of taking them away.

hints: Add the hour first, then the minutes, and change any 60 minutes into an hour. Or round the film to 2 hours and correct for the extra minutes at the end.
17:45 plus 1 hour is 18:45. Adding 15 minutes reaches 19:00, and 35 more minutes are still to add.

solutions.reliable: Add the hour: 17:45 becomes 18:45. Now add 50 minutes in two steps: 15 minutes takes the clock to 19:00, and the other 35 minutes take it to 19:35. The transferable idea: when adding times, jump to the next full hour first, since an hour has 60 minutes.
solutions.elegant: 1 hour 50 minutes is 10 minutes less than 2 hours. Two hours after 17:45 is 19:45; take off 10 minutes to get 19:35.

whyOnTest: Time arithmetic tests working in sixties instead of hundreds, a unit slip that costs many students easy points.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
